title: Joint Consistency: A Unified Test-Time Aggregation Framework via Energy Minimization
claim: Existing aggregation methods using isolated scores or votes pick wrong answers; modeling global pairwise interactions recovers the correct one.
layout: 3 sections, left-to-right: traces table, judge pairwise matrix, method comparison table
description: A left-to-right worked example on a single math problem. On the left, a black-header table lists six candidate answers (2, 254 with a red star, 128, 128, 0, 4) and the model that generated each. An arrow leads through a Judge Model box with an OpenAI logo. The center panel shows a blue column of independent scores P(y_i) and a green upper-triangular matrix of pairwise preference probabilities P(y_i ≻ y_j). Another arrow leads to the right-hand table, Test-Time Aggregation. Its columns are SC, BoN, WSC, KT and JC, with blue headers for independent signals and green headers for comparative signals. Yellow cells mark each method's chosen answer. SC, BoN, WSC and KT highlight wrong answers. JC picks 254 (energy -3.580) and is marked with a red star.
caption: TTA methods on crowdsourced traces for Q28 from the HMMT 2025 (Nov) dataset, where the ground-truth answer is 254. Yellow cells denote the final aggregated answer selected by each method. Blue and green cells represent independent evaluation signals and comparative signals, respectively. The right table reports the answer-level scores used by each method: SC counts supporting traces, BoN takes the highest independent score, WSC sums independent scores, KT records the tournament round reached, and JC computes the energy in [ref]. Higher scores are preferred, except for JC, which minimizes energy. SC, BoN, and WSC favor incorrect majority or high-scored answers. KT eliminates the correct answer 254 in Round 2 after losing to 128 with a pairwise score of 0.4. In contrast, JC with $\mu=0.5$ successfully identifies the correct answer by aggregating global pairwise interactions.
abstract: This paper studies test-time aggregation, an approach that generates multiple reasoning traces and aggregates them into a final answer. Most existing methods rely on evaluation signals collected from candidate traces in isolation or answer frequencies, while ignoring comparative interactions among candidates. We propose Joint Consistency (JC), formulated as a constrained Ising-type energy minimization problem, which employs both independent evaluation signals and pairwise comparisons using LLM-as-a-judge. JC provides a unified framework for test-time aggregation that subsumes typical voting and weighted aggregation methods as special cases. Moreover, we develop an efficient approximation strategy that makes interaction modeling practical for large-scale test-time aggregation. Experiments on math and code reasoning benchmarks show that JC outperforms existing baselines across tasks, judge models, trace budgets, and trace-generation settings, with particularly pronounced gains on challenging problems.
